profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC16 data center at 44740 Performance Circle in Ashburn, Virginia, one node in Equinix's cluster of buildings spread across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC16 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 249,787 square feet of space, N+1 power redundancy, and eight compliance certifications, HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. That footprint makes DC16 markedly larger than several of its Equinix siblings on this same campus, DC4 at 60,590 square feet and DC6 at 59,374 square feet, though Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC16 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and it markets DC16 alongside DC15 as providing connectivity into what it calls extensive interconnection ecosystems for network exchange customers, without breaking out DC16's own cross connect count or customer base publicly.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
DC16 is a 250,000-square-foot facility on Equinix's Ashburn campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, one of roughly 330 mapped data centers in the state. The operator does not publish DC16's total power capacity, but the facility is rated for 5 kW per rack, a density suited to general colocation rather than high-density AI training. At this density, a fully populated building of this size could support roughly 300 to 400 racks depending on usable space allocation; assuming 40 kW per rack for AI training workloads, such capacity would represent 12 to 16 MW of AI-capable IT load, but this remains a calculation from power density, not from published total capacity.

DC16 sits within Ashburn's Data Center Alley, a region of roughly 10 million square feet of total data center space anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own DC1 and DC2 facilities from the late 1990s. Equinix positions this campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, with emphasis on internet exchange access, cross-connects, and interconnection products. Among Virginia's 23 facilities with published megawatt figures, this campus ranks 24th, suggesting it is not among the state's largest disclosed capacity players.

The facility offers N+2 cooling redundancy and generators with extended runtime, standard qualifications for financial services and regulated workloads requiring high availability. DC2, held as representative of the campus's general specifications, carries HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High certifications, though these are not confirmed specifically for DC16. For an operator positioning capacity around connectivity and colocation services rather than announcing new power build-out, this facility appears marginal to the question of whether AI compute is binding against power constraints in Virginia.
